confirmed.title: M17: pid_output_limit clamps commutation lead angle below 90 deg when max PWM voltage < 64, reducing torque vs old firmware
confirmed.detail: pid_output_limit = new_max_motor_pwm_voltage << 8, and the anti-windup block (lines 2356-2371) hard-clamps the returned output to +/-pid_output_limit. The M17 caller (lines 2589-2599) uses the raw output as the commutation lead angle up to HALL_TO_POSITION_90_DEGREE_OFFSET = (64*1024)>>2 = 16384 counts, THEN derives voltage as output>>8. The comment's claim 'beyond this output, neither the commutation angle nor the PWM voltage can increase any further (M17 semantics)' is only true for max_pwm >= 64 (64<<8 = 16384). Failure scenario: user sends Set-max-motor-current with value 32 (legal range 0..390, checked at line 3370) for a torque-limited move; pid_output_limit = 8192, so under load the lead angle saturates at 8192 counts = 45 deg instead of 90 deg -> torque proportional to sin(angle) drops to 71% of old firmware at identical PWM voltage (38% at max_pwm=16, i.e. 22.5 deg). Loads that moved under fw 0.15.2 at low current limits now stall or trip the position-deviation fatal error. Fix: clamp output at max(pid_output_limit, HALL_TO_POSITION_90_DEGREE_OFFSET) on M17, or use the true saturation point max_pwm<<8 only when it exceeds 16384. Verified against Src/commutation_table_M17.h (N_COMMUTATION_STEPS=64, N_COMMUTATION_SUB_STEPS=1024) and MAX_PWM_VOLTAGE_AT_ZERO_VELOCITY=390 (motor_control.c:57).

confirmed.title: recompute_pid_parameters_and_set_pwm_voltage zeroes previous_error, producing an avoidable one-tick derivative kick on every Set-PID-constants / Set-max-motor-current during motion
confirmed.detail: previous_error = 0 in the critical section means the next TIM16 tick computes error_change = error - 0, i.e. the full current position error (clamped to max_error_change) instead of ~0. Measured with extracted firmware code at M17 defaults (p=2000,i=5,d=175000,V=200): motor holding steady error 3000 counts, then recompute() with UNCHANGED constants -> output jumps from 10261 to 11868 (+1607 counts = 3.1% of full 51200 authority, 15.7% of the running output), decaying over ~1 ms; worst case is max_error_change*deriv_scaled>>11 = 599*5468>>11 = +/-1599 regardless of gains. The reset is unnecessary for overflow safety: previous_error is always a previously-clamped value in +/-2^29, so (error - previous_error) fits in int32 for ANY new constants; only the low_pass_filtered_error_change reset (line 2201) is needed (stale lpf meeting a larger derivative constant). Fix: delete line 2202 (or set previous_error to the entry-clamped current error is not possible here; simply keeping it is safe). Scenario: host adjusts torque limit (set_max_motor_current, line 3377) while the motor tracks a trajectory under load -> visible/audible jerk each command.

confirmed.title: Integral gain silently capped ~50-500x below commanded value when P is zero or very small
confirmed.detail: The new ki cap (lines 2181-2187) computes ki_max = (INT32_MAX - new_max_integral_term) / new_max_error. When pid_p == 0, new_max_error stays at the full authority (line 2164-2167), so ki_max collapses. Concrete scenario: M17, max PWM voltage 200 -> authority = 200<<19 = 104.8e6; user sends Set PID constants with p=0, i=1000 (pure-integral tuning experiment): ki_max = (2147.4e6 - 26.2e6)/104.8e6 = 20, so integral_constant_pid becomes 20 instead of 1000 with no error or indication -- the motor integrates 50x slower than commanded (worse at higher voltage settings). The old code used the commanded ki directly (though it could overflow, which is what this cap prevents). A tighter error clamp applied only to the integral accumulation path would preserve the commanded gain instead of silently rewriting it; at minimum the cap deserves a fault/flag so tuning tools are not misled.
